The name symbolizes the release from worldly attachments and the attainment of spiritual freedom. The name Muksidul carries the meaning “Liberation from bondage” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Muksidul usually hope their child will grow to embody liberation from bondage and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Muksidul was the name of a Jain monk who lived during the Pala Empire (750-1200 AD). He was a great scholar and preacher, and is credited with the authorship of several Jain texts.

Another reference to Muksidul comes from the 12th century Jain text 'Kalpa Sutra', where he is mentioned as a prominent Jain teacher and the founder of the Digambara sect's main monastery in Bundelkhand.
